## Eleventh Army subordination to Mackensen

**Sources on this page:** p101 A2, p101 D2. [Concise case study](../military/mackensen_subordination.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p100 D1](100.md#source-p100-d1).

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-subordination-eleventh-army-subordination-to-mackensen"></a>



Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

A two-part telegram on Childs pp100–101 reports that the 11th Army and all
its German elements have been placed under `O.K. MACKENSEN` and asks for
orders. A second copy of the ending provides useful letter evidence but has
an extra five-coordinate group and a weak source glyph. The native reading
and the conditional copy analysis remain distinct.

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-subordination-p100-d1"></a>

### p100 D1

The [D1 source](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p100_D1.png)
reads `UKS v ZON`, received at an unspecified time on November 2, origin
`2312 (1) 2 TLE`, and `1 TL RICHI-136`. There are 136 slots, including the
printed `L` at source 39 and `C` at 56. The following page is explicitly
marked as a continuation.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame**

```text
OXKXMACKENSENX11XARMEE?ITALLENDEUTSCHENTEILENISTLAUT?XHXLXRMX1A11127
```

**Edited output — explicitly priced coordinate repairs and mask fills**

```text
OXKXMACKENSENX11XARMEEMITALLENDEUTSCHENTEILENISTLAUTOXHXLXRMX1A11127
```

</details>

**Readable German — from the edited layer**

> O.K. Mackensen. 11. Armee mit allen deutschen Teilen ist laut O.H.L. RM 1A11127

This first part has 66/68 raw fixed positions. Filling `L39` as `D` and
`C56` as `A` gives 68/68 fixed positions with **no observed-coordinate
substitutions**. It ends in reference `RM 1A11127`, with the sentence
continuing in A2. The source does not supply additional words between the
reference and that continuation.

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-subordination-p101-d2"></a>

### p101 D2

The [D2 source](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p101_C1_D2.png)
reads `UKS v ZON`, `2.15 a.m., November 2nd`, origin `2352 (1)`, and
`2 TL RIZI-137`. Its origin differs from A2's `2312`. This edition reserves
**137 source slots**, including printed `S` at 19 and an illegible fifth
slot after `XDVV` at 119. The latter is not transcribed as the copy's expected
`X`. The [14× detail](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p101_D2_illegible.png)
shows a separate upper stroke and lower ink trace in that slot. The advertised
137 supports this interpretation but is not its only evidence. In the source
JSON, `?` at this one location explicitly denotes an illegible ink remnant,
not a printed question mark.

The common-frame model excludes the **five observed coordinates** in
`XDDAF`, source 10–14, to obtain 132 slots. Those exclusions have a cost of
five observed-coordinate operations; they are not free padding removal.
All native 137-slot diagnostics, including the unpaired coordinate, remain
in the certificate.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 132-slot copy-alignment frame**

```text
?EMOXKXMACKENSENUNTERSTELLTUNDBI?TETUMBEFEHLEXAXOXKX11XRMX1A70G1XX
```

**Edited output — same conditional frame; separately priced exclusions**

```text
DEMOXKXMACKENSENUNTERSTELLTUNDBITTETUMBEFEHLEXAXOXKX11XRMX1A7011XX
```

</details>

**Readable German — from the conditional edited layer**

> dem O.K. Mackensen unterstellt und bittet um Befehle. A.O.K. 11. RM 1A7011.

This model has 64/66 raw fixed positions. The selected edited text fills
`S19`→`G` and the illegible source 119→`X`, and changes source 136 `F`→`X`.
The last substitution changes the raw reference `70G1` to `7011`, supported
by A2's unchanged coordinate. Its price is **1 observed substitution,
2 source-mask fills and 5 observed-coordinate exclusions**.

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-subordination-equal-cost-copy-readings"></a>

#### Equal-cost copy readings

After the declared alignment, the two endings have 128 identical observed
coordinates, two complementary masks, and two observed conflicts. At common
frame index 65, A2 has `V` and D2 has `F`; at 131, A2 has `X` and D2 has `F`.
There are four equally minimum common streams:

| Common word / reference | A2 substitutions | D2 substitutions | Combined substitutions |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `BITTEP / 7011` | 0 | 2 | 2 |
| **`BITTET / 7011`** | **1** | **1** | **2** |
| `BITTEP / 70G1` | 1 | 1 | 2 |
| `BITTET / 70G1` | 2 | 0 | 2 |

Every row additionally uses the same two D2 source-mask fills and the
separately stated five exclusions. The chosen readable row combines the
`T` supported by D2 and the numeric reference supported by A2. Equal edit
cost alone does not select it, and the two physical copies do not prove
independent transmission histories.

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-subordination-geometry-and-weak-glyph-limits"></a>

#### Geometry and weak-glyph limits

All **133 contiguous five-coordinate exclusions** in the 137-slot source
were evaluated against the selected common text. Starts **8, 9, 10, 11 and
12** tie at one observed substitution and give exactly the same raw and
edited streams. Their source-origin maps differ. Start 10 is the printed
group boundary used for presentation, not a unique historical loss or
insertion location. This finite test does not exhaust arbitrary five-coordinate
exclusions or alternative plaintexts.

The old OCR's **136-slot interpretation** is retained as an alternate
reading of the weak ink trace. Under that interpretation, the equivalent
132-slot copy model needs five observed exclusions, one newly supplied
coordinate, one source-mask fill and one substitution. It produces the same
final text. The text therefore cannot decide whether the weak fifth slot
was a printed character or a missing coordinate; the primary slot choice
comes from the image review.

## Parallel Orient reports on South-Slav units

**Sources on this page:** p101 B2, p101 C1. [Concise case study](../military/orient_south_slav_reports.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p102 B1](102.md#source-p102-b1), [p102 B2](102.md#source-p102-b2), [p102 B3](102.md#source-p102-b3).

<a id="edition-cases-military-orient-south-slav-reports-parallel-orient-reports-on-south-slav-units"></a>



Prepared by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**.

Childs pp101–102 preserve closely related reports on South-Slav units near
Montenegro. The p102 report is an explicitly numbered three-part message.
The p101 material has a damaged first part and a matching detachment passage,
but some headers and wording differ. The edition preserves each physical
record instead of merging those differences.

<a id="edition-cases-military-orient-south-slav-reports-p101-c1"></a>

### p101 C1

The [C1 source](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p101_C1_D2.png)
reads `UKS v ZON`, received at `3.15 a.m., November 2nd`, origin
`1225 (1) 3 TLE`, and `1 TL RICHI-190`. Its native 190-slot frame includes
32 printed dashes and a `C` at source 92. The fifth-row group is `GGGDA`,
with three visible `G` characters; its
[detail](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p101_C1_GGGDA.png)
prevents treating the second `G` as an additional mask.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame**

```text
NO?MEC?E?SEN?NA?H?ORI?NTB?R?CHT?OM???10X?IOD?S?EDS?AVI??HEX?INH?I?EN5?NXM??TE8?GRO?V?RGE?UEC??X
```

**Edited output — explicitly priced coordinate repairs and mask fills**

```text
NOXMACKENSENXNACHXORIENTBERICHTVOM??X10XSINDXSUEDSLAVISCHEXEINHEITENVONXMONTENEGROXVORGERUECKTX
```

</details>

**Readable German — from the edited layer**

> N.O. Mackensen. Nach Orientbericht vom ??.10. sind suedslavische Einheiten von Montenegro vorgerueckt.

The candidate has **93/95 fixed positions**, after five observed-coordinate
substitutions and 31 source-mask fills. The two date positions remain
unknown; the visible `10` is retained. Raw `5` in `5?N` and `8` in
`M??TE8?GRO` are locally priced word repairs toward `VON` and `MONTENEGRO`;
they do not assign any historical number. The beginning stays literal `NO`
(rendered `N.O.`), without changing it to a different headquarters abbreviation.
The word `EINHEITEN` fits the partially visible `?INH?I?EN` and is also
present in the related p102 B1 report.

The passage says that South-Slav units have advanced **from** Montenegro.
The corresponding p102 B1 text below says **in** Montenegro. The source
coordinates support this wording difference. The p102 date `28` is not
transferred into the two unresolved p101 positions.

<a id="edition-cases-military-orient-south-slav-reports-p101-b2"></a>

### p101 B2

The [B2 source](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p101_A2_B2.png)
reads `UKS v ZON`, `3.23 a.m., November 2nd`, and `2 TL RICHI-200`.
Its own origin number is absent. A relationship with C1 is plausible from
the topic, part number and nearby reception times, but is not established
by an identical complete header. The last group is `GVXDC`; the final
[`C` at source 199](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p101_B2_C199.png)
is a mask, not a silently chosen `G`.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame**

```text
WAHRSCHEINLICHDASXAUSDERXSUEUSLAVISCHENXDIVXGEBILDETEXDETACHEMENTX2RGTRXIVFX2RGTRXKAVXMITG?BIRGSARQL
```

**Edited output — explicitly priced coordinate repairs and mask fills**

```text
WAHRSCHEINLICHDASXAUSDERXSUEDSLAVISCHENXDIVXGEBILDETEXDETACHEMENTX2RGTRXINFX2RGTRXKAVXMITGEBIRGSARTL
```

</details>

**Readable German — from the edited layer**

> Wahrscheinlich das aus der suedslavischen Div. gebildete Detachement. 2 Rgtr. Inf. 2 Rgtr. Kav. mit Gebirgsartl.

This is 99/100 fixed raw and 100/100 fixed after three observed substitutions
and one mask fill. It describes a detachment probably formed from the
South-Slav division: two `Rgtr. Inf.`, two `Rgtr. Kav.`, with mountain
artillery. The abbreviations remain in the display; their unit numbers are
literal. The related p102 copy supports the masked source coordinate and
several differing letters, with the equal-cost limitations recorded below.

<a id="edition-cases-military-orient-south-slav-reports-p102-b1"></a>

### p102 B1

The [p102 B source](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p102_B.png)
prints an unavailable station pair, an unspecified reception time on
November 3, and `1227 ZON (1/11) 3 TLE`. Its first part is
`1 TL RICHI-208`, with 208 valid coordinates.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame**

```text
ABTXFRXHEEREXGDXHXQUXSXMXNACHXORIENTBESICHTXVOM28X10XSINDSUEDXLAVISCHEXEINHEITENINMONTENEGROVORGERUECKTX
```

**Edited output — explicitly priced coordinate repairs and mask fills**

```text
ABTXFRXHEEREXGDXHXQUXSXMXNACHXORIENTBERICHTXVOM28X10XSINDSUEDSLAVISCHEXEINHEITENINMONTENEGROVORGERUECKTX
```

</details>

**Readable German — from the edited layer**

> Abt. Fr. Heere. G.D.H.Qu.S.M. Nach Orientbericht vom 28.10. sind suedslavische Einheiten in Montenegro vorgerueckt.

All 104 raw labels are fixed. Two observed substitutions, source 82 `X`→`V`
and 168 `V`→`A`, repair `SUEDXLAVISCHE` and `BESICHT`. No masks or geometry
changes are needed. Its recipient and administrative abbreviations differ
from p101 C1. `GDXHXQUXSXM` is punctuated as `G.D.H.Qu.S.M.` without expanding
its letters. The source date is the literal `28.10.`.

The shared subject makes the parallel useful, but `1225`/`1227`, the recipient
strings, the date evidence and `VON`/`IN` remain separate. This is not treated
as an exact re-encryption of the whole first part.

<a id="edition-cases-military-orient-south-slav-reports-copy-agreement-and-extra-shared-word-repair"></a>

#### Copy agreement and extra shared-word repair

The two detachment records have **192 identical observed coordinates**,
**seven observed conflicts**, and **one complementary mask**. All
**128 minimum common streams** are preserved in the certificate. Their
aggregate substitution cost is seven, and they all retain the shared raw
word error `SUEUSLAVISCHEN`.

The chosen complete candidate costs three substitutions in p101 B2 and
six in p102 B2, for **nine combined substitutions**, plus the one p101 source
mask fill. The two operations above the minimum are the additional shared
source-44 change `A`→`G`, once in each copy, to obtain `SUEDSLAVISCHEN`.
Thus the fluent word is an additional priced repair; the copies do not
independently confirm it through an unchanged coordinate. The body wording,
unit labels and all individual conflicting values remain inspectable.

<a id="edition-cases-military-orient-south-slav-reports-p102-b3"></a>

### p102 B3

The third part is `3 TL RICHI-192`. It has 192 valid coordinates. The
[detail of `VGDGD`](../../experiments/nov1_mackensen_and_orient_reports/sources/p102_B3_VGDGD.png)
shows a `D` at source 152, not an invalid `L`; no fill is charged or claimed
at that position.

<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame**

```text
AUSXAGEDESXSERBISCHENOFFIZIERSDER3BATTR3FELDARTLRGTSXDONAUDIEXNXOX11NR2429VOM19X10XVODOHL11X0626
```

**Edited output — explicitly priced coordinate repairs and mask fills**

```text
AUSSAGEDESXSERBISCHENOFFIZIERSDER3BATTR3FELDARTLRGTSXDONAUDIEXNXOX11NR2429VOM19X10XVODOHL11X0626
```

</details>

**Readable German — from the edited layer**

> Aussage des serbischen Offiziers der 3 Battr. 3 Feldartl. Rgts. Donaudie. N.O. 11 Nr. 2429 vom 19.10. VODOHL 11. 0626.

All 96 raw positions are fixed. One observed substitution, source 51
`X`→`V`, supplies `AUSSAGE` in place of `AUSXAGE`. The passage attributes
the report to a Serbian officer and gives the literal designations
`3 BATTR 3 FELDARTL RGTS`, followed by `DONAUDIE` and reference strings.
`DONAUDIE` is not silently converted to a different unit abbreviation, and
`VODOHL` remains unexpanded. The numbers `3`, `11`, `2429`, `19.10.` and
`0626` keep their exact encoded forms, including the leading zero.
